minutes.headline: Sewer Commission drafted proposed ADU sewer connection fees and tie-in rules but took no final vote on them.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission spent most of the meeting workshopping a proposed regulation and fee structure for Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) sewer connections, comparing draft language from a commissioner and from staff, and discussing tie-in methods, easements, metering, and billing scenarios without taking a formal vote on the policy. The commission also voted to approve prior minutes, voted to credit a resident's sewer bill after a water-meter-driven billing error, and previewed upcoming agenda items including two easement waiver requests and a flow-increase vote for a change of use.

what_happened.line: Commission drafted ADU sewer connection fees and tie-in rules but took no final vote, planning one consolidated draft before town council.
Commission voted to credit a resident's sewer bill after a water-meter change had inflated her usage reading.
Draft rule discussed: an ADU line must tie into the existing house line, not connect directly to the street, or pay a full new-connection fee.
Commission previewed two upcoming easement waiver requests and a flow-increase vote for a retail space becoming a gym.

why_it_matters: Anyone adding an accessory dwelling unit will owe a sewer connection fee that is still being drafted, not yet set or voted.
A water-meter change can move a sewer bill on its own, as this credit shows, without any error by the resident.
The change-of-use flow vote and easement waivers ahead touch how much sewer capacity other properties can claim.
watch_next: Next Sewer Commission meeting: consolidated ADU fee draft for discussion before it goes to town council
Future meeting: flow-increase vote on the retail-to-gym change of use and two easement waiver requests
